title: Geometry optimization of monolayers
action: For each monolayer (SnSe, SnS, GeSe, GeS), perform DFT geometry optimization using Quantum ESPRESSO with GGA (PBE) and a van der Waals correction to obtain relaxed lattice parameters and atomic coordinates.
description: Initial structure optimization required for all subsequent calculations.

title: Electronic structure and effective masses
action: For each optimized monolayer, perform self-consistent and non-self-consistent band structure calculations on a uniform k-point mesh to obtain electronic eigenvalues and direction-dependent effective masses (armchair/zigzag).
description: Provides eigenvalues for BoltzTraP and effective masses for mobility calculation.

title: Elastic constant and deformation potential
action: Compute the 2D elastic constant C2D by fitting energy vs. uniaxial strain, and the deformation potential constant E1 from the shift of the conduction band minimum under strain, using DFT.
description: Parameters needed for deformation-potential mobility theory.

title: Carrier mobility and relaxation time
action: Using C2D, E1, effective masses, and temperature, compute carrier mobility and relaxation time for armchair and zigzag directions at 300 K, 500 K, and 700 K via deformation potential theory.
description: Provides temperature-dependent relaxation times needed as input to BoltzTraP.

title: Electronic thermoelectric properties via BoltzTraP
action: Run BoltzTraP2 with the electronic eigenvalues and the temperature-dependent relaxation times to obtain Seebeck coefficient (S), electrical conductivity (σ), and electronic thermal conductivity (κe) as functions of carrier concentration and temperature (300–700 K) for both directions.
description: Generates the raw electronic transport functions needed for Seebeck and ZT extraction.

title: Maximum Seebeck coefficient at 300 K
action: From the BoltzTraP output, determine the maximum absolute Seebeck coefficient (over doping and direction) at 300 K for each monolayer and write the value to `seebeck_max_300K.csv`.
description: Extracts the largest Seebeck coefficient at room temperature.
output_schema: Columns: composition (string), S_max (float, μV/K). One row per compound.

title: Phonon harmonic IFCs and band structure
action: Using Phonopy with a supercell (e.g., 5x5x1) and Quantum ESPRESSO forces, compute the second-order interatomic force constants and the phonon dispersions for each monolayer.
description: Harmonic IFCs needed for lattice thermal conductivity; phonon dispersions verify stability.

title: Phonon stability (no imaginary modes)
action: From the phonon dispersion output, extract the minimum phonon frequency (real/imaginary) for each compound and write to `phonon_stability.csv`.
output_schema: Columns: composition (string), min_frequency (float, THz). One row per compound.

title: Anharmonic third-order IFCs
action: Compute third-order interatomic force constants using a supercell (e.g., 4x4x1) and interactions up to the 15th nearest neighbour, using the `thirdorder.py` script from ShengBTE.
description: Anharmonic IFCs required as input for ShengBTE.

title: Lattice thermal conductivity via ShengBTE
action: Run ShengBTE with the harmonic and anharmonic IFCs to solve the phonon Boltzmann transport equation, obtaining lattice thermal conductivity (iterative and SMRTA) as a function of temperature and direction.
description: Generates κl(T) data needed for the lattice thermal conductivity and ZT comparison.

title: Room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity
action: From the ShengBTE output, extract the lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K for armchair and zigzag directions of each monolayer and write to `lattice_thermal_conductivity.csv`.
output_schema: Columns: composition (string), direction (armchair/zigzag), kappa_l (float, W/m/K). Rows for each compound and both directions.

title: Thermoelectric figure of merit ZT at 700 K
action: Using the electronic transport properties (S, σ, κe) from BoltzTraP at 700 K and the lattice thermal conductivity κl from ShengBTE at 700 K, compute ZT = (σ S²) / (κe + κl) × T for each material and direction; report the maximum ZT over doping in `zt_700K.csv`.
description: Reproduces the maximum ZT values at 700 K.
output_schema: Columns: composition (string), direction (armchair/zigzag), ZT (float). Rows for each compound and both directions.
